parsed_answer.content:
Virtual Threads, introduced in Project Loom, represent a paradigm shift in Java concurrency by decoupling Java threads from OS threads, allowing for millions of concurrent tasks. However, this shift breaks the fundamental assumptions of ThreadLocal. In a traditional platform thread model, ThreadLocal variables are safe because a thread is expensive and long-lived, effectively acting as a container for request-scoped data. With Virtual Threads, the sheer volume of threads makes the 'one-thread-per-request' model problematic if ThreadLocal is used, as it leads to massive memory bloat and potential data leaks if threads are not properly cleaned. Because virtual threads are frequently created and destroyed, the overhead of managing ThreadLocal maps—which are inherently mutable and unbounded—becomes a performance bottleneck and a source of memory pressure.

Scoped Values, introduced as a preview feature, are the modern replacement designed specifically for this high-concurrency environment. Unlike ThreadLocal, which is mutable and persistent for the life of a thread, Scoped Values are immutable once bound and are designed to be inherited by child threads automatically. They solve the 'unbounded lifetime' problem by restricting the scope of the data to a specific execution block. When the block finishes, the binding is implicitly cleared. This makes them perfectly suited for Virtual Threads, as they eliminate the need for manual cleanup and prevent the accidental leakage of data across unrelated tasks that might share a carrier thread.

items: ThreadLocal relies on a ThreadLocalMap stored within the Thread object. In a Virtual Thread environment, if you have 100,000 threads, you potentially have 100,000 maps, even if most are empty or contain only a few references.

Scoped Values are designed to work with Structured Concurrency. When a parent thread spawns a child virtual thread, the Scoped Value bindings are effectively 'pushed' down to the child, ensuring context propagation without the performance tax of copying maps.

Because Scoped Values are immutable, they eliminate the data races inherent in ThreadLocal where one part of the code might modify a value that another part of the same thread expects to remain constant.
The JVM optimizes Scoped Values by storing them in a way that is accessible to the current thread's stack, avoiding the heap-heavy overhead of the ThreadLocalMap.

parsed_answer.content: Senior Insight: Do not attempt to migrate large legacy ThreadLocal implementations to Scoped Values blindly. ThreadLocal is often abused as a 'global variable' container. Scoped Values enforce a strict lexical scope; if your application architecture relies on setting a value in a filter and reading it deep in the DAO layer without a clear parent-child execution boundary, Scoped Values will force a refactor. Furthermore, remember that Scoped Values are immutable; you cannot 'update' them, you can only 'rebind' them for a nested scope.

title: How do Virtual Threads change the way we use ThreadLocal? (Scoped Values)
